assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Spontaneous fission
items.clue: Fission of a nucleus without any particle being absorbed.

items.label: Nuclear fusion
items.clue: The joining of two light nuclei to form a heavier nucleus.

items.label: Nuclear fission
items.clue: The splitting of a heavy nucleus into two smaller nuclei of comparable mass (the fission fragments), usually with the release of two or three neutrons and energy.

items.label: Instability strip
items.clue: A narrow, nearly vertical band of the HR diagram that extends upward from the main sequence through the giant and supergiant regions, at intermediate surface temperatures.

questions.stem: A reactor core is surrounded by thick layers of steel and concrete. What is the main purpose of these layers?

options.text: To absorb the neutrons and γ radiation leaving the core, protecting people nearby
To stop α particles from the fuel, the most ionizing and most harmful radiation
To contain the explosion if the chain reaction runs out of control, as in a bomb
To keep thermal energy in the core, so that less is wasted to the surroundings

questions.explanation: Neutrons and γ rays are penetrating and escape from the fuel and reactor vessel. Thick steel and concrete absorb them so that people outside the reactor receive only a very small dose. This is the shielding.

questions.stem: Spent fuel contains caesium-137 (half-life 30 years), strontium-90 (half-life 29 years) and technetium-99 (half-life 2.1 × 10⁵ years), produced in similar numbers by fission. Which conclusion about the long-term storage of this waste is correct?

options.text: After about 60 years, two of their half-lives, the caesium-137 and strontium-90 in it have completely decayed.
Most of its activity at first comes from technetium-99, as it has by far the longest half-life of the three.
Burying it deep in rock reduces its activity, since the rock absorbs the radiation that the waste emits.
It stays radioactive for far longer than 300 years, as the technetium-99 barely decays in that time.

questions.stem: The spectrum of a star is a continuous spectrum crossed by dark lines. Two of the dark lines are at wavelengths that match lines in the emission spectrum of sodium measured in the laboratory. What do these two dark lines show?

options.text: Sodium is absent from the star, so light at those two wavelengths is missing.
The lines are produced by sodium atoms in the star emitting light at those wavelengths.
Sodium in the star's outer layers is absorbing light of those two wavelengths.
Sodium is being made by nuclear fusion in the core of the star itself.

questions.explanation: Continuous radiation from deeper, hotter layers passes through the cooler outer layers. Sodium atoms there absorb their own characteristic wavelengths, so dark lines at the sodium wavelengths show that sodium is present in the outer layers.

questions.stem: Proxima Centauri, the nearest star to the Sun, has a parallax angle of 0.768 arc-second. Take 1 pc = 3.09 × 10¹⁶ m and 1 ly = 9.46 × 10¹⁵ m. What is its distance from the Earth in light-years?

An HR diagram is drawn with luminosity on the vertical axis (increasing upwards) and surface temperature on the horizontal axis (decreasing to the right). A star in the upper right of the diagram has a luminosity of 5.0 × 10⁴ L⊙. Its spectrum peaks at a wavelength of 725 nm. Take L⊙ = 3.83 × 10²⁶ W, σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴ and Wien's displacement law λ_max T = 2.9 × 10⁻³ m K. The star is modelled as a black body. What is its radius?

An HR diagram is drawn with luminosity on the vertical axis (increasing upwards) and surface temperature on the horizontal axis, running from 40 000 K at the left-hand end to 2500 K at the right-hand end. Star P is plotted at the lower left of the diagram, well below the main sequence. Which description of star P is correct?

options.text: A white dwarf: hot, but tiny, so its luminosity is low.
A cool red star, dim because its surface temperature is low.
A young dwarf that will later swell into a red giant.
A Sun-sized star that is dim because it has nearly run out of fuel.
